test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The sign of acceleration depends on its direction relative to velocity. Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Acceleration is positive if it is opposite to the direction of velocity.
Acceleration is always positive, irrespective of direction.
Acceleration is negative if it is in the direction of velocity.
Acceleration is positive if it is in the direction of velocity, and negative if it is opposite.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Acceleration is positive if it is in the direction of velocity, and negative if it is opposite.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **Acceleration** is a **vector quantity** defined as the **rate of change of velocity** of an object with respect to **time**. Because it is a vector, it has both **magnitude** and **direction**.

• The **sign** of acceleration (positive or negative) is determined by the **direction** of the **acceleration vector** relative to the **velocity vector** and the chosen **coordinate system**.

• When an object is **speeding up**, the **acceleration** acts in the **same direction** as the **velocity**. In standard physical conventions, if the velocity is moving in the positive direction, this acceleration is considered **positive**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

• If the **acceleration** is directed **opposite** to the direction of **motion (velocity)**, the object **slows down**. This is known as **negative acceleration** or **retardation**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
